about: MUTATING — creates or replaces ONE repository ruleset on GitHub that protects the branches matching a pattern, and nothing else (infra/forge/github-act.sh set-branch-protection). Design 76155676 decision 4 (David 2026-09-27: GitHub acts are bounded verbs, plan then passkey-approved write, each proving by reading GitHub back; backlog 6a8ff89f). A ruleset rather than classic branch protection because the classic endpoint takes one branch NAME and cannot carry a pattern such as publish/**. AUTHORISED PER RUN BY DAVID'S PASSKEY in design 17835005's shape: it declares requires_approval with plan-a-github-branch-protection as its plan_verb, so the runner renders the plan onto the request's approve step, runs this only after a passkey on the approvers list signs those bytes, and hands the script sha256 of the SIGNED plan; the script re-renders from GitHub and acts only while the bytes hash alike. Its bound is the script's: the verb owns exactly one ruleset per pattern, named `boss: refs/heads/<pattern>`, created (POST) or replaced whole (PUT); it never touches a ruleset it did not name and never deletes one; the rules are FIXED in the script — creation, update (restrict updates), deletion, non_fast_forward, plus required_status_checks when checks are named — so a request chooses only who may push (bypass actors app:<App id> or team:<team id>, or none: nobody) and which checks — a check name carrying a space, comma or parenthesis spelled with %XX escapes (the mirror's `Gate (infra/gate.sh, full)` is Gate%20%28infra%2Fgate.sh%2C%20full%29), which the plan prints decoded — each optionally PINNED to the App that must run it as <name>@<App id>, GitHub's integration_id (backlog 16a9c5ae: unpinned, any App that can write checks satisfies it with a run of that name, and publish-github-pr --merge refuses to merge over an unpinned requirement; the mirror's Gate runs under GitHub Actions, App 15368, so main's check is Gate%20%28infra%2Fgate.sh%2C%20full%29@15368). A rulesets API has no user actor, so an identity is an App or a team. IT REPLACES A CLASSIC RULE ON THE BRANCH IT NAMES (backlog 602fe95f, David 2026-09-30: only the GitHub App updates the public mirror's main): GitHub applies classic branch protection beside a ruleset, and main's classic rule required checks (`rust`, `web`) no workflow produces, which would bind the App whatever the ruleset said. So when the pattern is one branch name, the plan reads GET /repos/<owner>/<repo>/branches/<branch>/protection and prints it, and the act DELETEs it only after the ruleset reads back, proven by that read answering 404 Branch not protected; a pattern (publish/**) is not read, and the plan says so. It authenticates as the GitHub App's INSTALLATION on <owner>, from the slot /etc/boss-publish/github-app/<owner>.token the forge converge renders from the broker's installation token (per-owner data, never a constant); a slot that is absent, loose, not root's, empty or expired is a refusal before GitHub is called, and the token is never printed. Proof: the ruleset reads back, normalised, equal to the plan — one that does not is exit 1. Any other 4xx or 5xx is exit 1 naming GitHub's words.
effect: ^github-act: proven — ruleset .+ reads back as desired
